notes: Non-discriminating: 15 of 16 assertions passed in both configurations. Opus without the skill finds planted overclaims on its own; finding issues is not where the skill adds value.
Only discriminating assertion: a claims registry the checker accepts (with-skill 1/1, baseline 0/1). The skill's value is the durable, machine-checked artefact and the CI gate, not detection.

Skill defect 1 (meshwatch): the checker requires tests for 'partial', so in a repo with no tests every claim with real code was forced to 'absent', contradicting SKILL.md's own edge-case rule and losing information.
Skill defect 2 (meshwatch): OC-6 led the run to list the computed ManifestBadge 'VERIFIED' as a (minor) overclaim, a false positive the baseline avoided.
Cost: +85% time and +27% tokens with the skill.
Baselines found unplanted issues (MASTER_KEY never loaded, no AAD binding, failed reads logged as reads); with-skill matched most of them.

Report files: in 3 of 4 runs the harness refused subagent writes of report .md files; the evaluator saved each run's final reply verbatim as its report. claims.json/CLAIMS.md were written by the runs themselves.
Trigger test (separate, simulated): 20/20 correct routing among 11 skills; claude -p was unavailable so run_eval.py was not used.
